milestone: CDC age 5: uses or recognizes simple rhymes
mechanic: Adult fills a basket with 10 to 12 small household objects that form rhyming pairs (sock and rock, cat toy and hat, spoon and moon picture, car and jar, bear and chair from a dollhouse, can and pan). Child pulls one object, says its name, and hunts in the basket for the object that rhymes. Pairs go side by side on the table. Harder round: adult says a word, child finds an object that rhymes with it. Hardest: child invents a nonsense rhyme (sock, lock, mock, zock).
safety_points: Use objects larger than a toilet paper tube opening if younger siblings are around.

milestone: CDC age 5: recognizes simple rhymes; hops on one foot
mechanic: Child stands at one end of a hallway or yard. Adult says two words. If they rhyme (cake, lake), the child hops forward one hop on one foot. If not (cake, dog), the child stays still or does a silly freeze pose. Reach the finish line to win. Swap roles: child calls the word pairs. Variation for older kids: three words, hop if all three rhyme.
safety_points: Clear the path of toys and rugs that slip. Hop on carpet or grass, not tile in socks.

milestone: Kindergarten phonological awareness: breaking words into syllables
mechanic: Clap the beats in family names (Ma-ya = 2 claps, Ben = 1 clap, Ol-i-ver = 3). Then foods at dinner, animals, toys. Child guesses how many claps before clapping. Movement version: stomp, jump, or tap knees for each beat. Sorting version: put toys into 1-clap, 2-clap, 3-clap piles.

milestone: CDC age 5: writes some letters in their name; names some letters
mechanic: Adult writes the child's first name in big letters on a strip of cardstock (capital first letter, then lowercase, the way kindergarten teaches it). Child cuts between letters with kid scissors (or adult cuts with wavy lines so pieces fit like a puzzle). Child rebuilds the name, first with a model strip to match, then without. Next steps: trace the letters with a finger, then copy two or three letters with a crayon. Do the same for a sibling's or pet's name.
safety_points: Child-safe scissors with an adult at the table.

milestone: CDC age 5: writes some letters; pre-writing strokes
mechanic: Pour a thin layer of salt (or sugar, or cornmeal) into a baking sheet or shallow box lid, about a quarter inch deep. Optional: colored paper underneath so letters show bright. Child draws lines, circles, zigzags with one finger, shakes the tray to erase. Then letters of their name and numbers 1 to 5, copying from a card. Adult can draw a letter, child guesses it, then they swap. Use a paintbrush or chopstick as a pencil for grip practice.
safety_points: Keep salt away from eyes; wash hands after. Do it at the table, on a towel.

mechanic: Adult sews one big button (about 1 inch) to the end of a ribbon and ties a knot or felt stopper at the other end. Cut 8 to 10 felt squares (2 to 3 inches) with a slit in the middle of each. Child pushes the button through the slit of each square and slides it along the ribbon, making a long snake, then unbuttons them off. Start with a big button and long slits, move to smaller buttons and tighter slits. Bridge to real clothes: practice on a parent's cardigan laid flat on the table, bottom button first.
safety_points: Sew buttons on firmly and check them before each play. Keep loose buttons away from children under 3.

mechanic: Two piles of oversized clothes at the far end of the room: a button-up shirt, a zip jacket, a hat, socks. Each player runs to the pile, puts everything on (buttons included), runs back, takes it off, and the next player goes. Solo version: race the timer and try to beat yesterday's time. Easier: only hat and jacket; harder: all buttons done up and shoes on the right feet.
safety_points: No running in socks on hard floors. Skip scarves and anything with drawstrings around the neck.

milestone: CDC age 5: hops on one foot; counts to 10; names numbers
mechanic: Draw a classic hopscotch grid 1 to 10 with sidewalk chalk (indoors: painter's tape on the floor). Toss a stone or beanbag on a square, hop on one foot on single squares and land with two feet on side-by-side squares, skip the square with the marker, pick it up on the way back. Number games: hop and call out each number, hop only on even numbers, adult calls a number and child hops to it.
safety_points: Check for traffic and slick spots before drawing. Use a beanbag indoors, not a stone.

milestone: CDC age 5: does simple chores, like matching socks
mechanic: Dump a load of clean socks on the bed. Child finds pairs by color and pattern, folds or rolls each pair, then sorts pairs into piles by family member (biggest feet to smallest). Count the pairs. Add a challenge: race the timer, or find the sock with no partner. Turn it into a weekly job with a small paper chart.

milestone: CDC age 5: follows rules and takes turns; counts
mechanic: On a large sheet of paper, draw a winding path of 20 to 30 squares from START to FINISH. Child decorates and adds a few special squares (slide back 2, jump ahead 3, do 5 jumping jacks). Use small toys as playing pieces and one die. Roll, count the dots, move that many squares, counting each one out loud. Talk about rules before playing and what happens when you lose. Later: two dice and add them, or a spinner made from a paper clip.

milestone: CDC age 5: pays attention for 5 to 10 minutes; plays card games with rules
mechanic: Make 12 to 16 cards from index cards: draw simple pairs (sun, apple, house) or use stickers. Shuffle face down in a grid. Players take turns flipping two cards; keep a pair, flip back if they don't match. Start with 6 pairs, grow to 10. Variations: match letter to picture (B and ball), number to dots, rhyming pairs.

Fill a clear bin or sink with water. Collect 10 objects (spoon, cork, apple, coin, leaf, crayon, sponge, toy car, plastic lid, rock). Draw a two-column chart: SINK and FLOAT. Child holds each object, predicts, drops it in, and places it in the right column. Talk about surprises (the apple floats, the small coin sinks). Extra round: make a sinking object float (put the coin in a plastic lid boat) or a floating object sink (squeeze water into a sponge).
safety_points: Adult stays at the water at all times and empties it right after play. Coins and small objects away from younger siblings.

milestone: CDC age 5: counts to 10; names numbers 1 to 5
mechanic: Each player has a pile of blocks (building blocks, plastic cups, or brick-style bricks). Roll one die, count the dots, add that many blocks to your tower. First to 20 blocks wins, or play cooperatively and build one tower together until it falls. Count the tower out loud after each turn. Harder: roll two dice and add; or roll and take away.
safety_points: Keep small bricks away from children under 3.

milestone: CDC age 5 tip: memory and attention games like Hot and Cold
mechanic: One player hides a small toy while the seeker waits outside the room. Seeker searches; the hider guides only with 'warmer', 'colder', 'hot', 'freezing'. Swap roles so the child practices giving clues. Variations: clap faster when close instead of words; use spatial words (behind, under, next to) as hints; hide three items in a row.
safety_points: Agree on no-go spots: ovens, high shelves, outside the house.
